sections.h2: What should York, PA sellers know before listing?
sections.html:
York is a compact city of 5.3 square miles in York County, and its Bureau of Permits and Inspections decides several things a seller needs before closing, including tenant licenses and a possible certificate of compliance. The paperwork runs through an online permit system, and the office takes appointments only.

The Census Bureau estimates 45,342 residents for July 2025, up 1.2 percent from the 2020 base. Its 2020 to 2024 survey shows 43.7 percent of homes lived in by their owners, a middle value of $119,700 and typical rent of $1,014 a month across 17,893 households. Median household income is $48,420, and 21.1 percent of residents are in poverty.

York was founded in 1741, became a borough in 1787 and a city in 1887. The Continental Congress met in the courthouse from September 1777 to June 1778 and adopted the Articles of Confederation there. Colonial-era buildings and large Gothic churches still stand around town.

sections.h2: Which York City documents does a house sale or rental need?
sections.html:
York City Bureau of Permits and Inspections document types, as described on the Bureau's permits page
DocumentWhen it applies
Tenant occupied licenseTenant-occupied residential and institutional buildings, which are inspected before licensing
Certificate of ComplianceA structure changing ownership or tenancy without a change in use classification
Certificate of OccupancyNew construction, major renovations, reoccupying condemned structures, changes in occupancy
Electrical turn on permitNeeded before the utility restores service, with a DR number from Met-Ed

The permits page says a Certificate of Compliance applies to any structure that changes ownership, while its FAQ describes it for existing commercial buildings. Call the Bureau at 717-849-2256 to confirm what a house sale requires. The office is at 101 S. George St., and the page states that it cannot take walk-in customers, so appointments are made by phone.

Permits have also moved to the 2021 Uniform Construction Code for applications filed from January 1, 2026.

Before any inspection, collect the deed, any prior certificates, receipts for permitted work and the names of every tenant. York City says permit applications must be filed before work begins, so have those records ready.

sections.h2: What does a tenant occupied license mean if I am selling a rental in York?
sections.html:
Owners of rental houses in York carry a license that depends on an inspection, and the city says no checklist exists. Inspectors apply the City of York Property Maintenance Code, which is posted on the city website, so landlords read the code itself to prepare.

  • Reinspections and the Consolidated Board of Appeals go through the tenant occupied administrative desk.
  • Typical complaints in the city include weeds over 10 inches, uncollected trash, pest problems, leaks, sewer backups and mold.
  • Neighborhood Improvement Ordinance tickets can be appealed, but the appeal form has to be mailed or hand-delivered, not emailed.
  • Property owners are responsible for the sidewalk and trees in front of the house.

A buyer who purchases rentals as is will usually want the current license and any open citations in hand before settlement. Clear those, or disclose them in writing, ahead of the contract.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded and taxed in York County?
sections.html:
York County's Recorder of Deeds says the realty transfer tax is 2 percent in total, with 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to local governments. Documents go first to the county Assessment Office, which certifies the parcel number, and then to the Recorder for recording and fees.

  • You can record in person, by mail, or through Simplifile or Ingeo, with a stamped return envelope and payment for the fees.
  • One check may cover everything, or you can write three, and the county accepts either.
  • A Statement of Value is required when you claim an exemption or pay a different amount than the deed states. It adds $2 to the recording fee.
  • A deed from a father to a son and similar family transfers are tax exempt if the deed states the relationship.
  • Recorded documents come back after about four to eight weeks, depending on workload.

The state notes both buyer and seller are liable for the tax, and the sales contract decides who pays. Ask the Recorder for the share that applies to a York City address.

sections.h2: Which schools and neighborhoods influence York home values?
sections.html:
York sits inside the York City School District, one of 15 public districts across the York area, and charter options include Lincoln Charter School and Helen Thackston Charter School. York Catholic High School and Holy Trinity Catholic School are among the private options. York College of Pennsylvania, Penn State York and the Harrisburg Area Community College York campus add student renters and staff.

The Arch Street area holds WellSpan Park, home of the York Revolution since 2007, and the old Pennsylvania Railroad station now sits on the York County Heritage Rail Trail across from the stadium. The York County Judicial Center and new apartment lofts anchored later redevelopment downtown. Spring Garden and West Manchester townships border the city, and several of the area's large employers are based in them.

sections.h2: How do local employers and roads affect York sellers?
sections.html:
York has deep manufacturing roots. The area is home to a Harley-Davidson plant, Voith Hydro, BAE Systems, York International and a Starbucks roasting facility, and Dentsply Sirona and Glatfelter moved their headquarters out in 2019 and 2020. WellSpan York Hospital, a regional trauma center, and UPMC Memorial Hospital serve the city.

US 30 and Interstate 83 cross the area, Rabbit Transit runs bus routes in the city and suburbs, and a Greyhound and Trailways depot offers intercity service. The nearest commercial airports are BWI and Harrisburg International, with Lancaster's Amtrak service about 24 miles east. The Census gives a mean commute of 23.1 minutes for York workers, so sellers can market access to both Harrisburg and Baltimore.

sections.h2: Does York's weather or flood history matter when I sell?
sections.html:
The city has hot, humid summers and moderately cold winters. Rain and snow add up to about 41 inches a year, falling on roughly 127 days. Hurricane Agnes set the state's 24-hour precipitation record of 13.5 inches at the York weather station on June 22, 1972, so buyers do ask about basements.

Plan to show a dry basement and sound gutters, and keep records of sump pump work or waterproofing. An as-is purchaser prices roof and foundation questions differently from a buyer who needs a loan, so say plainly what you know.

Gather permit records for past work too. Electrical, plumbing, mechanical and demolition work in York City goes through the Bureau's online system, and sheds, decks and interior remodels need permits as well.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell my York house?
faqs.a: Possibly. York City says a structure changing ownership or tenancy without a change in use needs a Certificate of Compliance, though an FAQ on the same site ties it to commercial buildings. Call 717-849-2256 to confirm for your address.

faqs.q: How much does York County charge in transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent in total, with 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to local governments, according to the county Recorder of Deeds. The sales contract decides whether buyer or seller pays.

faqs.q: Can I transfer a York house to a family member tax free?
faqs.a: Yes, when the deed states the family relationship, such as a transfer from a father to a son. The county advises checking with an attorney, and a Statement of Value is needed if you claim any other exemption.

faqs.q: How do I get a permit or license from York City?
faqs.a: Most applications are filed online through the city's OpenGov system. The Bureau of Permits and Inspections, at 101 S. George St., also takes appointments by phone at 717-849-2256.

faqs.q: How long until York County returns my recorded deed?
faqs.a: It takes about four to eight weeks after recording, depending on workload, because each document is scanned, proofed, indexed and verified. Include a stamped, self-addressed envelope.
